modes.label: Pitching too early
modes.lesson: You described the product before the buyer described the problem, so you learned nothing you can use.

modes.label: Leading question
modes.lesson: You put the answer in the question. The buyer agreed politely and you still have no evidence.

modes.label: Our number, not theirs
modes.lesson: A benchmark from other customers is not evidence. Only the buyer's own number survives a business case.

modes.label: Accepting a vague answer
modes.lesson: The buyer gave you a direction, not a number, name or date. Push once more before you move on.

modes.label: Single-threading
modes.lesson: You moved the deal forward through one person without testing whether they have power.

modes.label: Coach treated as champion
modes.lesson: Enthusiasm is not authority. A champion shows access, influence and a personal stake before you lean on them.

modes.label: Right question, wrong person
modes.lesson: The question is good, but this buyer cannot answer it. Ask the person who owns it.

modes.label: Closing too early
modes.lesson: You asked for commitment before the buyer agreed the problem, the value or the path. It cools the room.

modes.label: Feature dump
modes.lesson: Features answer a question the buyer did not ask. Tie every capability to their outcome or leave it out.

modes.label: Discounting before value
modes.lesson: A price move before the value is agreed tells the buyer your first number was not real.

modes.label: Unbounded pilot
modes.lesson: A pilot with no end date or exit gates becomes a free trial nobody finishes.

modes.label: Trashing the alternative
modes.lesson: Attacking the alternative makes you sound defensive. Ask what it would take for them to choose it instead.

modes.label: Paper process left to the end
modes.lesson: Legal, security and procurement run in parallel with the evaluation or they add months after it.

modes.label: Over-promising
modes.lesson: A guarantee you cannot control costs credibility the moment the buyer tests it.

modes.label: Vanity metric
modes.lesson: Usage and satisfaction are not outcomes. The buyer needs a number their executive already tracks.

modes.label: Handing over control
modes.lesson: An open question to a busy executive wastes their time. Lead with a point of view and let them correct it.

modes.label: Not listening
modes.lesson: The buyer just told you what matters to them, and you moved past it.

modes.label: Going around your contact
modes.lesson: Contacting their boss behind them burns the relationship you need most.

modes.label: Working around the veto
modes.lesson: A veto holder you avoid becomes a veto holder you meet at the end, angry.

modes.label: Assuming authority
modes.lesson: You assumed who signs instead of asking. Assumptions about authority are where forecasts break.

modes.label: Vendor template, not their plan
modes.lesson: A plan the buyer did not build is a plan the buyer will not follow.

modes.label: Lowering the bar
modes.lesson: Negotiating the buyer's standard down signals you cannot meet it.

modes.label: Fake urgency
modes.lesson: A deadline you invented gives the buyer a reason to distrust everything else you said.

modes.label: Rate card instead of their cost
modes.lesson: A rate card makes the buyer do your work. Translate the unit into cost per piece of their work.

modes.label: Average customer, not this one
modes.lesson: Their volume, growth and peaks are the forecast. An average customer is a guess.

modes.label: Oversized commit
modes.lesson: A commit above proven usage looks like a discount and lands as shelfware.

modes.label: Burying the answer
modes.lesson: Executives decide in minutes. Lead with the recommendation, then the reasons.

modes.label: No recommendation
modes.lesson: Options without a recommendation hand your job back to the executive.

modes.label: Fear without numbers
modes.lesson: Risk with no number attached sounds like every vendor. Quantify it in their terms.

modes.label: Dodging governance
modes.lesson: Structuring a deal to avoid the buyer's controls tells them you will cut corners elsewhere too.

modes.label: Signature as the finish line
modes.lesson: In a consumption deal, signature is halftime. Name the first users and their first week.

modes.label: Generic value claim
modes.lesson: Best in class means nothing to a buyer. Name the before, the after and the proof.

modes.label: Getting defensive
modes.lesson: Defending the product before you understand the concern makes the concern bigger.

modes.label: Deferring the hard part
modes.lesson: Pushing the hard question past the next milestone guarantees it surfaces at the worst time.

modes.label: Negotiating against yourself
modes.lesson: Offering to come back with a better number before they ask for one invites a lower price.

modes.label: Commit without a forecast
modes.lesson: A commit that is not built from the buyer's own volumes is a guess. Finance will cut it, or the buyer will pay for usage they never reach.
